dedupe_keys.name: chime agent based model of hurricane information flow and evacuation

description: The Communicating Hazard Information in the Modern Environment (CHIME) agent-based model is a NetLogo program for analysing information flow and protective decisions across space and time during hazardous weather. It tests hypotheses about collective human responses to forecasts, using real geography and hurricane data to set the simulation bounds and historical National Hurricane Center forecast information to start the flow of forecasts to citizen agents. Version 2.1.0 updates the model first published by Joshua Watts, adding new hurricanes, a reader for the newer National Hurricane Center forecast format, Florida census data that can modify agent behaviour, and detailed code documentation and optimisation. It was published on the CoMSES Computational Model Library in January 2022 by Sean Bergin, C. Michael Barton, Joshua Watts, Joshua Alland and Rebecca Morss, last modified in December 2024, is peer reviewed with an Open Code Badge, and is downloadable under GPL-3.0 and runs on any operating system with NetLogo. Associated papers appear in the Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society (2017) and Environmental Modelling and Software (2019). Caveats: behaviour rules are stylised, and the census extension covers Florida. It supports agent-based emergency response and evacuation modelling and the design of warning systems; a related record is the US National Response Framework.
